answer: The system resists Sybil attacks through per-identity insurance staking, where each identity locks 50 units for 30 days and loses that stake if a jury finds copied work. To activate, the owner carries its token across a river on foot in one timed trip, winds it 10 turns along a spiral ramp where each turn is logged, and sets it beside an ivory marker weighing 200 grams on a scale at the top. A missing crossing, a count under 10 turns, or a weight off by more than 5 grams voids activation, so 100 fakes need 100 trips and 5,000 locked units.
